plan.contextChunk: This figure contains six panels (a)–(f) illustrating the operation of insertion sort on an array of six integers. Each panel shows a horizontal array of six cells indexed 1 through 6 above the cells. Gray cells to the left of the current key represent the already-sorted subarray; the current key is shown in a black cell with white text; white cells to the right remain unsorted. Curved arrows below the array indicate element movements: a bold black arrow points to the slot where the key will be inserted, while lighter gray arrows indicate elements shifting one position to the right to make room. Panel (a) shows the initial array [5, 2, 4, 6, 1, 3] with key 2 at position 2 moving left past 5. Panel (b) shows key 4 at position 3 being inserted into sorted subarray [2, 5]. Panel (c) shows key 6 at position 4 requiring no movement as it is already the largest element in the sorted prefix. Panel (d) shows key 1 at position 5 shifting four elements rightward to reach position 1. Panel (e) shows key 3 at position 6 shifting three elements rightward to reach its correct position. Panel (f) shows the final sorted array [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6] with no black cell and no arrows. This figure illustrates the insertion sort algorithm step by step, demonstrating how each key is extracted and inserted into its correct position within the growing sorted subarray to its left.

demo_steps.title: Full textbook figure
demo_steps.narration: The default view shows all six source snapshots in the original 2x3 layout. Black marks the key being inserted, while gray marks the specific elements examined or shifted in that panel rather than the entire sorted prefix.

demo_steps.title: Panel (a): insert 2
demo_steps.narration: The key 2 moves left ahead of 5, and the gray 5 is the element shifted right to make room.

demo_steps.title: Panel (b): insert 4
demo_steps.narration: The key 4 moves between 2 and 5. The gray cells show the source-highlighted comparison or shift context for this insertion, not every sorted cell by rule.

demo_steps.title: Panel (c): examine 5 before 6
demo_steps.narration: Only cell 3 is gray in the source panel because 5 is the examined value that confirms the key 6 can stay where it is. Cells 1 and 2 are already ordered but are not gray here.

demo_steps.title: Panel (d): insert 1
demo_steps.narration: The key 1 moves all the way to the front. The gray run marks the values shifted right as space opens for the key.

demo_steps.title: Panel (e): insert 3
demo_steps.narration: The key 3 moves into index 3. The source gray highlight is limited to cells 2 through 5, showing the examined or shifted neighborhood rather than shading cell 1 or the final cell 6.

demo_steps.title: Panel (f): sorted result
demo_steps.narration: The final panel shows the sorted array with no gray cells and no key cell. Completion is shown by the values themselves, not by shading the entire array.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: In this textbook figure, gray is a local trace annotation for the current insertion step, so it must be read panel by panel rather than as a generic sorted-prefix color.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Recreate the source-style figure first: a large 2x3 grid of six panels should occupy most of the SVG width, with any navigator controls kept compact so the panels stay close to textbook scale. Do not derive gray shading from the sorted prefix; use the fixed source pattern: panel (a) gray index 2, panel (b) gray indices 1 and 3, panel (c) gray index 3 only, panel (d) gray indices 2 through 5, panel (e) source gray span indices 2 through 5 only with the black key over index 3 and no gray at indices 1 or 6, and panel (f) no gray cells. Use light gray for source highlights, black for the key with white numerals, and white for all other cells. Make the curved arrows visually bold with noticeably thicker strokes, deeper loops around the array cells, and larger filled arrowheads to match the textbook arrows.

interactions.frame: one recorded step shows the whole six-cell array with index labels, the gray sorted prefix, the black active key, the compared pair if any, and the curved arrow for the most recent shift
interactions.success_check: the final array must be in nondecreasing order and each completed pass j must leave the prefix A[1..j] sorted while preserving the original multiset of values
interactions.teaches: The learner understands the order in which insertion sort compares adjacent elements, moves the current key left, and expands the sorted prefix until the whole array is sorted

demo_steps.title: Start with one sorted item
demo_steps.narration: The first element alone is already sorted. The algorithm begins at position 2 and treats that value as the key to insert into the sorted prefix on its left.

demo_steps.title: Move a small key left
demo_steps.narration: When the key is smaller than its left neighbor, compare returns true and shift moves the key one position left. This recreates the motion shown by the curved arrows in panels (a), (b), (d), and (e).

demo_steps.title: Stop when the prefix is ordered
demo_steps.narration: When the key reaches the front or is no longer smaller than its left neighbor, the pass ends and the gray sorted prefix grows by one cell.

demo_steps.title: Finish with the whole array sorted
demo_steps.narration: After the last key has been inserted, every position belongs to the sorted prefix and the array is [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], matching panel (f).

plan.keyInsight: Insertion sort is not sorting the whole array at once; each pass inserts one key into an already-sorted prefix, making that prefix one element longer.
plan.reconstructionNotes: Use a single replayable version of the textbook array rather than six static panels. Preserve the original visual language: six bordered horizontal cells, large serif-style numbers, indices 1 through 6 above the cells, gray sorted-prefix cells, a black active-key cell with white text, and white unsorted cells. During each comparison, outline the two compared cells; during each shift, draw a curved arrow below the array from the key's old position to its new position, with lighter gray arrows implying displaced larger elements. Show milestone labels (a) through (f) as the replay reaches the textbook states: initial key 2, key 4, key 6 with no shift, key 1 moving to the front, key 3 moving into place, and the final sorted array.

demo_steps.title: Full textbook figure
demo_steps.narration: The default view shows all six source snapshots in the original 2x3 layout. Each panel is a fixed milestone of insertion sort on the array [5, 2, 4, 6, 1, 3].

demo_steps.title: Panel (a): insert 2
demo_steps.narration: The key 2 moves left ahead of 5, while 5 shifts one cell to the right. The first two positions become sorted.

demo_steps.title: Panel (b): insert 4
demo_steps.narration: The key 4 moves between 2 and 5, shifting 5 right. The sorted prefix grows to three positions.

demo_steps.title: Panel (c): insert 6
demo_steps.narration: The key 6 is already larger than 2, 4, and 5, so no values shift. The key remains in place.

demo_steps.title: Panel (d): insert 1
demo_steps.narration: The key 1 is smaller than every value in the sorted prefix, so it moves all the way to the front while 2, 4, 5, and 6 shift right.

demo_steps.title: Panel (e): insert 3
demo_steps.narration: The key 3 moves left until it sits between 2 and 4. The values 4, 5, and 6 shift right to make room.

demo_steps.title: Panel (f): sorted result
demo_steps.narration: All six cells are shaded because the whole array is now sorted: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6].

plan.keyInsight: Insertion sort works by preserving a sorted prefix and inserting one key at a time into the only position where that prefix remains sorted.
plan.reconstructionNotes: Recreate the textbook figure first, not a code runner: show all six panels by default in a clean 2x3 grid with no trace log, no caption box, no editor, and no debugging highlights. Use identical array geometry in every panel: six horizontal cells, indices 1–6 above, centered values, thin black borders, light gray sorted/shifted cells, black key cell with white number, and white unsorted cells. Curved arrows should match the source convention: black arrows show where the key moves, gray arrows show values shifted one cell right. The optional navigator may dim or enlarge a selected panel, but the default state must preserve the complete six-panel static figure.

interactions.teaches: The learner reads the six fixed textbook snapshots as a pass-by-pass insertion-sort trace while understanding that gray follows the source panel's examined or shifted cells, not a computed sorted-prefix rule

demo_steps.title: Full textbook figure
demo_steps.narration: The default view shows all six source snapshots in the original 2x3 layout. Black marks the key being inserted, while gray marks the specific elements examined or shifted in that panel rather than the entire sorted prefix.

demo_steps.title: Panel (a): insert 2
demo_steps.narration: The key 2 moves left ahead of 5, and the gray 5 is the element shifted right to make room.

demo_steps.title: Panel (b): insert 4
demo_steps.narration: The key 4 moves between 2 and 5. The gray cells show the source-highlighted comparison or shift context for this insertion, not every sorted cell by rule.

demo_steps.title: Panel (c): examine 5 before 6
demo_steps.narration: Only cell 3 is gray in the source panel because 5 is the examined value that confirms the key 6 can stay where it is. Cells 1 and 2 are already ordered but are not gray here.

demo_steps.title: Panel (d): insert 1
demo_steps.narration: The key 1 moves all the way to the front. The gray run marks the values shifted right as space opens for the key.

demo_steps.title: Panel (e): insert 3
demo_steps.narration: The key 3 moves into index 3. The source gray highlight is limited to cells 2 through 5, showing the examined or shifted neighborhood rather than shading cell 1 or the final cell 6.

demo_steps.title: Panel (f): sorted result
demo_steps.narration: The final panel shows the sorted array with no gray cells and no key cell. Completion is shown by the values themselves, not by shading the entire array.

plan.keyInsight: In this textbook figure, gray is a local trace annotation for the current insertion step, so it must be read panel by panel rather than as a generic sorted-prefix color.
plan.reconstructionNotes: Recreate the source-style figure first: a large 2x3 grid of six panels should occupy most of the SVG width, with any navigator controls kept compact so the panels stay close to textbook scale. Do not derive gray shading from the sorted prefix; use the fixed source pattern: panel (a) gray index 2, panel (b) gray indices 1 and 3, panel (c) gray index 3 only, panel (d) gray indices 2 through 5, panel (e) source gray span indices 2 through 5 only with the black key over index 3 and no gray at indices 1 or 6, and panel (f) no gray cells. Use light gray for source highlights, black for the key with white numerals, and white for all other cells. Make the curved arrows visually bold with noticeably thicker strokes, deeper loops around the array cells, and larger filled arrowheads to match the textbook arrows.

discrepancies: The generated default view is compressed into the left half of the screenshot because a large title/narration/legend/control panel occupies the right side; the source figure is only the six textbook panels spanning the full width.

Panel spacing is much tighter than in the source, so labels such as (b), (c), (e), and (f) are crowded close to the preceding array instead of sitting in generous whitespace to the left of each panel.

The arrows are semantically present but do not closely match the source styling: the generated curves are shorter/tighter in some panels, arrowheads are more triangular, and the multi-arrow panels look more cluttered and less like the clean textbook arcs.
The overall scale of the six-panel figure is much smaller than the source in the default state, making the panels read more like a thumbnail than a drop-in replacement for the original figure.
The generated figure adds a title, explanatory text, legend, step controls, and snapshot selector that are not part of the source and visually dominate the composition in the screenshot.
evaluation.notes: The arrays, values, highlights, and insertion-sort arrows are largely semantically correct, but the default rendering is overly compressed and visually dominated by extra UI rather than matching the spacious textbook layout.
action_items: Make the default all-panels view occupy the full available figure area; move the UI below, collapse it by default, or reduce it so the source-like figure is not squeezed into a small left-side thumbnail.
Increase horizontal spacing between the three columns of panels so panel labels do not crowd the previous array and the layout more closely matches the source.
Tune arrow geometry and arrowhead shapes to better match the source: longer smooth arcs, source-like tapered heads, and cleaner separation of the gray shift arrows from the black key arrow.
Increase the default scale of the cells, numbers, and panel labels so the six-panel figure has the same visual prominence and readability as the reference.
